text:
Maya: Quick heads up, BrightPath POC just hit a billing spike during stress tests. They report portal shows "~5k credits" but api returned quota_exceeded 429s. Demo at risk.

Ravi: Which 429 detail? Any header dumps?

Maya: They sent: 
> {"error":"quota_exceeded","code":429,"detail":"credits_zero"}

Claire: I checked billing ledger for brightpath-poc: credits_remaining = 0 at 2026-03-02T14:02Z. Portal cache mismatch after yesterday's bulk import.

sre-oncall: Edge logs show for brightpath-poc: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-limit: 100
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 18
x-account-credits: 0
```
Rate limiter and credits both 0; primary cause credits exhausted.

billing-bot: Spend alert: brightpath-poc usage $980.12 threshold $500 at 2026-03-02T14:03:10Z. Credits on file: 0.

Maya: They need us to top up for the next hour for the demo.

Ravi: Can do manual grant: `redwood admin grant-credits --acct brightpath-poc --amount 6000 --reason "POC demo top-up"` Will wait for approval.

product-se: FYI, we should also explain streaming token accounting. Streaming includes partial tokens billed on flush; clients often undercount. SE playbook has examples.

Claire: Executed top-up after verbal approval: credits_remaining now 6000. Flushed cache.

sre-oncall: Bumped rate limit 100->500 for 2 hours.

Maya: Re-tested customer's curl and streaming works. Header shows x-account-credits: 5996.

Ravi: Filed ticket POCPAY-221 to add migration verification and portal/billing discrepancy alerts.

Maya: I'll send a quick note to customer explaining root cause and what we did. Also offering a follow-up with SE to walk token burn rates.

Claire: Also scheduling a post-mortem with infra to avoid future migration cache failures.

Maya: Thanks all. Please keep me posted if alerts reappear. :thumbsup:
